Our generalized posterior combines a reconstruction loss, which keeps the low-dimensional representation faithful to the observed data, with a within-cluster sum of squares in the latent representation, which encourages cluster separation. Posterior computation alternates between Gibbs sampling over partitions and gradient-based updates of the autoencoder network, with the learning rate estimated jointly. We illustrate the approach through simulation studies and applications to four benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Influenza A Virus as a Multivalent Active Particle: Statistical Mechanics of Binding, Motility, and Antiviral Design
papers.summary: In this contribution, we review existing multivalent models of Influenza A Virus (IAV) systems to study virion dynamics and design of multivalent entry blockers. We review existing biochemical estimations of the dissociation constants and catalytic activities of the two virion ligands [hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA)], which can be used to develop quantitative theories and experiments. Multivalent models are statistical mechanics frameworks for studying the simultaneous interaction of multiple reversible ligand-receptor bonds. They quantify the effects of both combinatorial entropy terms and single-molecule ligand-receptor affinities. Multivalent frameworks led to the rationale of superselectivity, the ability of probes to sense specific concentrations of conjugated receptors. Multivalent models guided the design of antiviral nanomedicines constituted by polymeric scaffolds conjugated with small molecules such as sialic acid receptors targeting the ligands on the surface of the virion. Importantly, neuraminidase is an enzyme that limits the number of host-guest bonds through receptor desialylation. Like active particles, neuraminidase activity enhances virion motility in the extracellular medium. Modeling the dynamics of Influenza A virions requires developing out-of-equilibrium multivalent models.
papers.comment: Review article. Authors listed in alphabetical order

papers.title: PoseRieFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Whole-Body Text-to-Pose Generation
papers.summary: We present PoseRieFlow, a compact flow-matching framework for text-conditioned generation of whole-body 3D human poses. Prior text-to-pose methods either neglect articulated hands or model rotations in Euclidean space despite their non-Euclidean geometry. PoseRieFlow instead formulates generation directly on the product manifold of SMPL-H joint rotations, learning a text-conditioned vector field that transports samples from an isotropic $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ Gaussian prior to the data distribution along Riemannian geodesics. A part-tokenized Diffusion Transformer aggregates the 52 joints into eight body-part tokens, allocating a dedicated token and nonlinear projector to each hand, and restores per-joint resolution through part-specific decoders, shortening the sequence while improving kinematic fidelity over per-joint tokenization. With only 21.6M trainable parameters, PoseRieFlow supports expressive SMPL-H generation with detailed hand articulation at a fraction of the scale of recent LLM-based generators. On PoseScript, it attains the lowest whole-body kinematic error among all hand-producing methods, with consistent kinematic gains from the Riemannian formulation over its Euclidean counterpart at every practical inference budget, while distributional and retrieval metrics remain comparable between them.

papers.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
papers.summary: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.

papers.title: An Adaptive Quantum Search Framework under Unknown Solution-density: Minimizing Expected Queries to the First Solution
papers.summary: Grover's algorithm provides a mathematically optimal quadratic speedup for unstructured search, yet its standard formulation relies on a critical prerequisite: prior knowledge of the target solution count to determine the number of algorithm iterations. Although numerous strategies have been developed to identify or bypass this parameter, comparing them directly is nontrivial. This study investigates and computationally optimizes 3 prominent frameworks: Boyer-Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp, Fixed-Point search, and Density Estimation Methods. Density-specific benchmarks select the best tested method and configuration to minimize expected first-solution queries under 2 initialization-cost conventions. To translate these theoretical benchmarks into practical utility, a hybrid quantum-classical adaptive framework integrating Hill-climbing-assisted Grover Adaptive Search with state-space density estimation modeled via the Wang-Landau algorithm is proposed as a potential use-case. This implementation operates directly on the optimized query methods established earlier. Analytical models support the approach; ideal simulations show 18.8%-63.4% lower mean accumulated query costs than the tested randomized and fixed-point baselines.

papers.title: Payload-Blind Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing with Phase-Injected Chirps in CE-OFDM
papers.summary: Constant-envelope orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CE-OFDM) preserves a unit-magnitude sample envelope, but its Hermitian-symmetric structure makes dedicated sensing pilots costly, and additive pilots disrupt this envelope. We show that injecting a known chirp, here a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence, into the CE-OFDM phase enables payload-blind bistatic delay-Doppler sensing without dedicated sensing frames or an explicit pilot power split: the residual carrier, given by the ensemble mean under the adopted payload model, becomes an implicit superimposed pilot for a receive-only node. A Doppler-aligned receiver integrates this reference coherently across frames while the payload residual averages down. In contrast, phase-domain injected training (PIT) frame averaging, designed for quasi-static channel estimation, loses about 32 dB for the simulated target with 16 averaged frames. Closed-form approximations characterize the payload-induced floor, known-cell detection probability and direct-path tolerance. In the noise-limited simulations, the receiver incurs a 2.8 dB detection gap relative to a payload-aware matched filter without interference cancellation and matches a dedicated-pilot benchmark of equal reference energy without its 53% frame overhead.

papers.title: Who Picks First? Compensatory Fairness When Equal Division Is Impossible
papers.summary: When indivisible objects, such as heirlooms or tickets to sports events, do not divide evenly among agents with equal claims, some agents must receive more objects than others. Can picking first compensate those with fewer objects? We propose two principles of compensatory fairness. An agent with fewer objects must not envy a larger bundle with any one of its objects removed, and priority advantages among agents with equally many objects must alternate rather than accumulate. Non-wastefulness, neutrality and an object-wise form of Maskin monotonicity characterize the draft rules, in which agents pick in a fixed sequence. Adding the two principles and envy-freeness up to one object singles out the block--snake draft, in which agents with fewer objects pick first in every round and each group's order reverses between rounds. Among draft rules, compensation is compatible with strategy-proofness, but envy-freeness up to one object is not: once at least two agents receive more than one object, no draft that satisfies it is even weakly strategy-proof, and with two such agents the conflict extends to all non-wasteful and neutral rules. When agents may be indifferent between objects, resolving each tie in favor of the earliest later picker who strictly cares preserves the draft's fairness guarantees and ensures efficiency under pairwise dominance.

papers.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have become a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, but their effectiveness still depends heavily on large volumes of demonstration data. In manipulation tasks, this dependence is compounded by structured spatiotemporal uncertainty in the action space: multiple nearby actions or trajectories may successfully solve the same task, while semantically equivalent demonstrations often unfold at different speeds. Standard pointwise supervision treats each demonstrated action as an exact target, imposing an unnecessary learning burden under such uncertainty. We present SURE, a data-efficient VLA training framework that explicitly models both spatial and temporal uncertainty. SURE augments a VLA backbone with a lightweight transposed-convolutional probabilistic action decoder that captures spatial uncertainty through local correlations among neighboring action bins. It further introduces Soft-DTW alignment supervision to accommodate local timing variations between predicted and demonstrated action chunks. Together, these two components reduce sensitivity to demonstrator-specific poses and execution timing, enabling more data-efficient action learning. We evaluate SURE on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation tasks. Even with only 10% of the demonstration data or 20% of the training steps, SURE achieves manipulation success rates that match or surpass baseline VLAs.

papers.title: Vertically-coupled microring resonators for lithium niobate on insulator integrated photonics
papers.summary: We propose and demonstrate lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) microring resonators that are verticallycoupled to index-matched silicon-rich silicon nitride (SiN x ) access waveguides as an alternative to conventional lateral coupling schemes for integrated photonics applications. The wafer-scalable fabrication process involves a planarization step exploiting a single-step and reproducible spin-coating of a SU-8 epoxy spacer layer which allows a controlled separation to be established between the resonator and its access waveguide. The resulting multimode and single-mode microring resonators exhibit, for their fundamental TE 0 mode, intrinsic quality factors of 4.0 x 10 5 and 3.4 x 10 5 , respectively.

papers.title: The Multiscale Single-Index Model: An MSE Analysis of Online SGD Dynamics
papers.summary: We consider the Multiscale Single-Index Model (MSIM), first introduced by Oymak and Soltanolkotabi (2021), as a stylized model for hierarchical feature learning with scale separation. Each layer extracts a shared single-index feature at one physical scale and passes it to the next, giving a tractable setting in which to study how deep architectures learn local multiscale representations. Under non-degeneracy and delocalization assumptions on the link function and planted features respectively, for the two hidden-layer case ($K=2$), we analyze joint online spherical SGD under MSE loss, which is a canonical regression objective, in discrete time and show that it achieves weak recovery from random initialization in $O(d\log^2 d)$ samples, followed by strong recovery to accuracy $\varepsilon$ in $O(d\log(1/\varepsilon))$ additional samples. The main technical challenge arises from the non-Gaussian learned features observed by the second layer. We address this challenge through a quantitative Gaussian comparison using delocalization, combined with sharp trajectory-level control of the coupled SGD dynamics. This work is a companion to Bruna (2026, arXiv:2607.03347), which studies recovery under a correlation objective for general $K$.

papers.title: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry Using Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Particle image velocimetry (PIV) reconstructs a flow field from the motion of tracer particles but the reconstruction quality is bounded by how well the flow structure of interest is resolved in the images. The acquisition position is typically fixed by the operator before the measurement. We cast camera placement as a sequential decision-making problem and train a reinforcement learning agent to control a 6-DoF manipulator equipped with a camera, enabling it to locate, frame and resolve a hydrofoil wake in a water tunnel. The agent commands the camera pose and observes the scene only through the velocity field and uncertainty estimated from time-separated image pairs. It is trained entirely in a photorealistic simulation of our water tunnel, with wakes generated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations of hydrofoils with varying profiles, positions and angles of attack. After zero-shot transfer to the real water tunnel, the policy reliably locates and frames the wakes of randomly placed hydrofoils. It resolves the wake at a higher resolution than a fixed camera view and with lower error in the measured flow statistics, in roughly half the time of a full scan and with far fewer image pairs.

papers.title: Calibrating demand models versus adjusting OD matrices with traffic counts: a controlled comparison
papers.summary: Traffic counts are routinely used to calibrate travel demand models, particularly when the origin-destination (OD) matrix is not observed directly. An important modelling decision is whether to adjust individual OD flows or the parameters of the demand model that generates them. The latter approach uses fewer parameters and preserves a relationship between zonal characteristics and demand, but its accuracy depends on the assumed model structure. We compare three established approaches using the same prior information, traffic counts and equilibrium assignment. They estimate five production-gravity coefficients, origin and destination adjustment factors, or individual OD flows. Synthetic experiments on the Eastern Massachusetts and Chicago Sketch networks allow recovery to be assessed against known demand under different forms of model misspecification. Calibrating the five-coefficient model gives better OD recovery and held-out link-flow prediction when demand follows its assumptions or a two-purpose gravity process. Its advantage declines or reverses when destination choice or production relationships vary across zones. Cellwise adjustment achieves the closest fit to calibration counts in 65 of 66 evaluated conditions, yet it recovers OD demand least accurately of the three approaches in 45 of them. These findings show that model parameterisation matters beyond calibration fit. For transport planning, traffic counts should be used alongside independent evidence on trip production and distribution when selecting and validating a demand model.

papers.title: Spin to Orbital Angular Momentum Conversion in the Neutron Nucleus Weak Interaction
papers.summary: The neutron nucleus weak interaction generates a small parity non conserving rotation of the neutron spin as the neutron moves through matter. This parity-odd neutron rotary power can reach up to 2.2e-3 rad * cm-1 for slow neutrons in 139La, which possesses a p-wave resonance at 0.7 eV where the parity-odd asymmetry is greatly amplified. This spin rotation must conserve total angular momentum. Here we show that this conservation occurs through neutron orbital angular momentum generation. We experimentally demonstrate that a neutron prepared initially in a longitudinal spin-orbit state experiences no change in total angular momentum.

papers.title: Local Inference for High-dimensional Time Series
papers.summary: Local stationarity provides a natural framework for time series whose dependence structure evolves smoothly over time. In high-dimensional settings, however, its classical definition can break down, as approximation errors accumulate across time-varying coefficients. To address this limitation, we introduce $(ε_n,δ)$-stationarity, a generalization of local stationarity that holds locally in time and allows approximation errors to grow with the dimension, and we combine it with local sparsity, which lets the set of relevant predictors change over time. We show that, for high-dimensional time-varying autoregressions, the rate of stationary approximation is driven by local sparsity, so that local sparsity governs not only estimation but also the stationary approximation itself. We then develop a \textit{local lasso} with time-varying penalties that selects relevant predictors and their periods of activity, and we derive error bounds that depend on the local sparsity, quantify the cost of nonstationarity, and guide penalty and bandwidth selection. For inference, we propose a desparsified local lasso based on local nodewise regressions and establish a linear representation with an explicit smoothing bias. Asymptotic normality then follows under two bandwidth conditions, one for coefficient variation and one for nonstationarity. Simulations and applications to macroeconomic and neuroscience data illustrate the methods.

papers.title: Nonlinear Fault Tolerant Control of Wind Turbine Pitch Systems: A Comparative Study
papers.summary: Electro-hydraulic pitch systems account for about one fifth of wind-turbine failures, motivating the development of resilient control strategies for fault mitigation. The study considers a large set of robust nonlinear control designs of different feedback principles and architectures, and assesses their fault-tolerant capabilities in comparison to each other and against the industrial standard, i.e. the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The implementation and tuning of each scheme is based on a high-fidelity simulator to ensure nominal performance, whereas each controller is deployed unchanged on an experimental apparatus that includes a full-scale electro-hydraulic pitch system. The comparative evaluation of the considered fault-tolerant solutions is carried out through several tests that cover nominal operation and twenty-five representative fault scenarios, including sensor, process, and actuator faults. The analysis highlights the trade-off between performance preservation under faults and increased actuator chattering. The experimental results show that introducing a dynamic input-reconstruction module into the design of the nonlinear controllers significantly reduces actuator chatter without compromising their fault-tolerant properties.

papers.title: Magnon-polaritons in terahertz resonators based on antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism
papers.summary: Terahertz magnon-polaritons in antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism are theoretically investigated using YFeO$_3$ as an example. Dispersion relations are obtained for the quasi-ferromagnetic and quasi-antiferromagnetic modes. It is shown that the intrinsic Fabry--Perot resonances of the magnetic slab provide strong coupling, but their low quality factor limits the cooperativity. The photonic crystal cavity increases the cooperativity of the quasi-antiferromagnetic mode from $C\sim6$ to $C\sim41$ at 300K and to $2.2\times10^3$ at 63K.

papers.title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, organizing continuous robot execution into separately predicted segments and thus introducing potential discontinuities at action-chunk transitions. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action-chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. Given visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioceptive information, ODEAction learns an action transition field defined over action space, where a transition vector characterizes the evolution rate of the current action with respect to evolution time. During execution, the model takes the current action as its initial condition and integrates the learned field using an ordinary differential equation (ODE), recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as an action head and does not depend on a specific vision-language backbone architecture. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real robots show that ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality over matched action-chunking baselines, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures, including appendix. Technical report

papers.title: Experimental Evaluation of High-Throughput Structure Predictions
papers.summary: High throughput computational databases such as Materials Project, the Open Quantum Materials Database, and Alexandria now each list on the order of 10^5 predicted stable compounds. However, the overall reliability of these predictions in terms of actual experimental synthesizability remains poorly understood. In this work we attempt to synthesize, via arc melting, 34 different predicted ternary compounds. The majority of these materials did not form in the predicted structure, instead resulting in disordered variants or multiphase mixtures. Four formed ordered structures not reported before, one of them at a composition reported earlier without a structure. We discuss both the failures and the successes, and identify simple filtering criteria that can help researchers avoid hypothetical materials that are unlikely to form.

papers.title: Goodhart in the Planner: Sampling-Based Control Exploits Rewards Learned from Human Preferences
papers.summary: Robots increasingly choose actions by searching against a reward model learned from human preferences, in model-predictive control or best-of-$N$ selection; we measure what this does to the true objective. On HalfCheetah and Hopper with crowd-sourced labels, and on Meta-World drawer-open and plate-slide with synthetic labels and blind labels from the two authors, harder MPPI search cuts true return by up to 76%: with human labels the drawer opens in 0 of 20 runs against 10 of 10 for the cloned policy the planner starts from, while held-out label accuracy stays at 0.75-0.97. On plate-slide human labels are exploited less than synthetic ones, and on window-open search helps. True return roughly follows how far the planner's weights move from its proposals ($\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}}$) for both weighting rules we test, and best-of-$N$ with a verifier from synthetic labels falls below a single noisy action. We prove that $χ^2$-regularized MPPI at a temperature set by the scorer's error spread on the proposals is worst-case optimal, that no positive gain can be certified once that spread exceeds the scorer's own, and that an episode's return splits exactly into per-step terms, of which the guarantee covers the selection terms. Calibrated from 100 proposal pairs ranked by true return (an oracle) on start states the evaluation never uses, this rule is the safest fix we test: with each of five independent sets it succeeds in every arm run and keeps on average 86-94% of the cloned policy's return on plate-slide and drawer-open, though it is cautious where search helps. Calibration from a person's comparisons cannot detect a bias the scorer learned from that person; correcting for the pairs people cannot tell apart, or a second person, limits the damage.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 4 figures. Equal contribution. Code and results will be released

papers.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
papers.summary: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. This symmetry breaking further induces polar anisotropy, with an intensity ratio reaching 2.36. We propose that asymmetric contributions from excitons to the second harmonic optical dipole may influence this behavior. These findings establish interlayer coupling as a critical mechanism for introducing inversion symmetry breaking and tuning the optical response of van der Waals heterostructures, providing a powerful strategy for photonics and optoelectronics in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Local Correlations Determine the Dephasing Threshold of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology
papers.summary: In this work, we try to understand the question of how to address the survival of band topology in the presence of dephasing. We investigate this question in the Kane-Mele $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological insulator. To determine the stability of the topological invariant we construct a single particle Hamiltonian that also provides identical correlation at the single particle level. The phase transition from topological to trivial is determined by the gap closing of this correlation Hamiltonian. This gap closing is related to purity gap. As a diagnostics we calculated the invariant directly and as a complementary diagnostic, coherent two-terminal transport through the auxiliary correlation Hamiltonian exhibits quantized conductance in the nontrivial region. This does not establish physical conductance under dephasing. Our results identify a predictive local criterion for the survival of single-particle topological structure under a specified noise channel.

papers.title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tanβ$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
papers.summary: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tanβ$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tanβ$, $1\le \tanβ\le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $κ$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|κ|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.

papers.title: Dual Architecture Fusion Vehicle Lidar 3D Target Detection
papers.summary: In this paper, a 3D backbone network (SpconvTransformer) based on the fusion of convolutional architecture branch and Transformer architecture branch is proposed. The convolution branch uses 3D sparse convolution and submanifold convolution to learn local voxel features and semantic information, and the Transformer branch uses the self-attention mechanism to model the remote relationship between voxels, uses the broad receptive field to capture rich context information, and complementing the advantages of the two architectures by fusing the local features extracted from the two branches and the global features solves the problem of limited receptive fields of 3D convolutional neural networks. The experimental results show that the average accuracy of SpconvTransformer in 3D object detection and bird's-eye view detection tasks reaches 81.45% and 88.09%, respectively, and the average directional similarity reaches 91.10%, which is significantly better than other existing algorithms.
papers.journal: M. Li, W. Jin, and Y. Sun, "Dual Architecture Fusion Vehicle Lidar 3D Target Detection," 2026 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Algorithms (CAIBDA), Tianjin, China, 2026, pp. 1-5

papers.title: How Much Conversation History Does an AI Agent Need?
papers.summary: How does using less conversational history change reader-token use and benchmark scores? We examine this question on 1,100 BEAM questions. We held the retrieval ranking and reader constant across five fixed passage budgets, and mean assigned scores rose as the passage budget grew. The score gain per additional token became smaller at the upper tested budgets. Answerable questions generally received higher scores with more context. Pooled abstention scores sometimes rose as the passage budget shrank. We also tested message retention in a controlled task with explicit conversational-state targets and compared retained user messages with token-matched recency. Qwen matched the full state more often for direct requirements when user messages were retained. Its full-state matching declined when answers depended on references to earlier offers. Mistral produced near-floor results across the retention conditions. A scoring audit leaves the correctness of BEAM answers unresolved. These experiments characterize the token and score consequences of the tested memory budgets. Reliable budget selection depends on retaining the evidence each question requires and validating the measure used to assess answer quality.

papers.title: Video2Asset: Online Construction of Persistent 3D Street-Scene Assets
papers.summary: Online 3D street-scene asset construction turns multi-view video into a continually updated scene of independently editable objects. The central challenge is to accumulate partial, intermittent observations under motion and occlusion without fragmenting identities or mixing evidence across objects. To address this challenge, we propose Video2Asset, an online framework for constructing persistent 3D assets from multi-view video. Using occupancy as an intermediate representation, we construct identity-aware observations with Historical Carrier Guidance for instance decoding and an identity encoder fusing instance-aligned 3D features with multi-view appearance. Accumulated-Evidence Association compares current observations with identity, geometric, and appearance evidence accumulated within asset records to determine identity inheritance and update world-coordinate states. We instantiate meshes from an asset library using these states and combine them with an occupancy-derived static background to support scene visualization, mesh replacement, object deletion, and trajectory editing. Experiments on several datasets demonstrate improvements in temporal identity consistency and asset quality across multiple occupancy models, including a 15.4% reduction in asset fragmentation on nuScenes with SGE.

papers.title: Radiation-driven melting and porous flow in the near-surface layer of an ice sheet
papers.summary: The ablation area of an ice sheet can undergo melting both directly at the surface and in the metre or so below the surface, due to the penetration and absorption of shortwave radiation. The fate of the meltwater has important implications for the mass balance of the ice sheet; some of it runs off into surface streams and eventually to the ocean, while some is stored in the porous `weathering crust', and can refreeze. We present a fluid-mechanical model to analyse the downward percolation and lateral drainage of the meltwater in the crust, and its influence on porosity, saturation, temperature and melting rate. Previous models have either ignored the possibility for lateral drainage, in which case the crust is always saturated with water, or have made ad-hoc assumptions about where and how the meltwater runs off. Through a series of analytical and numerical solutions to the model, we find that lateral drainage has the effect of controlling the water table within the weathering crust, which separates an unsaturated region near the surface from a saturated aquifer beneath. Under fluctuating weather conditions that induce melting and refreezing, the lateral drainage can result in the near-surface ice being more porous and also colder than is the case without lateral drainage. The model is able to predict the partitioning of the meltwater between surface and subsurface runoff, and refreezing, and has potential to be incorporated within larger-scale models of the ice-sheet mass balance.

papers.title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
papers.summary: In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.

papers.title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity and Semantics
papers.summary: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) connects information across documents through entity relationships to support relational reasoning. However, black-box access to GraphRAG systems can enable adversaries to reconstruct knowledge graphs and recover both structural connectivity between entities and the semantics of their relationships. Existing defenses lack formal privacy guarantees and provide limited protection against such reconstruction attacks. We propose RelGuard, the first differentially private framework for GraphRAG, which provides formal privacy guarantees by mitigating connectivity leakage and protecting relations and their semantic meaning through relation removal. We formalize relation differential privacy (relation-DP), which bounds the distinguishability of mechanism outputs according to the semantic distance between alternative relations while accounting for relation removal. Building on this definition, we develop a four-step defense mechanism that sanitizes source documents before GraphRAG indexing by perturbing relation predicates or removing their associated connectivity using the exponential mechanism. Experiments across three GraphRAG systems and two targeted reconstruction attacks demonstrate that RelGuard provides stronger protection against reconstruction attacks than four existing defense mechanisms while better preserving downstream utility.

papers.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
papers.summary: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. Achieving sub-microarcsecond accuracy requires unprecedented control over detector morphology, optical distortion, and astrometric measurement techniques. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The project focuses on precise calibration methods, including Young's fringe projection, to monitor pixel geometry and intra-pixel response across gigapixel-scale focal planes. By integrating these advancements, RETINA seeks to enable astrometric detection of Earth-mass exoplanets with a precision of few tens of micropixels on the focal plane. We discuss the technical strategies, laboratory validations, and system-level integration required to achieve these goals, emphasizing the synergy between detector technology, optical calibration, and mission design. These innovations pave the way for next-generation astrometric instruments capable of transforming our understanding of exoplanetary systems and dark matter dynamics.
papers.journal: International Conference in Space Optics 2026, Kyriaki Minoglou, ESA/ESTEC; Karine Mathieu, CNES; Nikos Karafolas, ESA/ESTEC; Fr{é}d{é}ric Bernard, CNES, Oct 2026, Sorrento, Italy

papers.title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Prompt learning adapts vision-language models such as CLIP by optimizing a short learnable prompt. The cross-entropy objective pulls this prompt toward base-class specialization, whereas generalization to unseen classes benefits from staying close to CLIP's zero-shot feature space. Because both objectives act on the same prompt, their gradients conflict at convergence, and in our experiments no single-prompt loss design clearly improves on the cosine baseline. We propose Decoupled Mode Connectivity (DMC), which gives each objective its own prompt. Starting from a base-trained prompt, DMC trains a specialization prompt and a generalization prompt, and merges their text features with a fixed coefficient at test time, at the inference cost of a single prompt. A linear mode connectivity (LMC) corridor in text-feature space keeps the classification loss low for every classifier interpolated between the two endpoints, and a Visual Anchor KL term preserves CLIP's zero-shot class-similarity distribution of each image during specialization. We further argue that such regularizers should satisfy class-permutation invariance (CPI), and show via Fano's inequality, in an idealized model, that violating CPI lower-bounds the drop in novel accuracy by a term proportional to the mutual information between the prompt and the base-class labels. Across 11 datasets, DMC improves the average harmonic mean of base and novel accuracy over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp, and its interpolation curves pass beyond the single-prompt operating point, shifting the base-novel frontier rather than trading along it. Code is available at https://github.com/IemProg/DMC.
papers.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 46 pages (10 main + references, appendix and checklist), 15 figures. Project page: https://iemprog.github.io/DMC/ Code:https://github.com/IemProg/DMC

papers.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
papers.summary: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.

papers.title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
papers.summary: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 10 figures, submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 (in review)

papers.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been increasingly adopted to fine-tune pretrained models with low computational cost and is therefore also preferred in the federated learning paradigm to reduce computational and communication overhead. In this work, we investigate the sparsely explored problem of the risk of private data leakage in LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers (ViTs), where low-rank updates weaken the gradient signal available to a server with access to individual client updates. We show that quality of reconstruction is limited by two coupled ambiguities: reduced information in LoRA gradients and missing spatial cues from frozen positional embeddings. To address this, we propose a spatially anchored generative inversion framework that incorporates server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings into ViT blocks during fine-tuning at clients. The resulting positional gradients act as layer-wise spatial anchors, providing additional positional cues, while the generative prior keeps reconstructions on a realistic image manifold, reducing duplicate-data and patch-permutation artifacts, {which produce similar gradients as those produced when the target client images are used}. Adding our proposed spatial anchoring to GIAS improves PSNR by 10.14 dB, SSIM by 0.45, and LPIPS by 0.098 on CIFAR-10, as well as PSNR gains of 7.83 and 11.74 dB on high-resolution CelebA and CARS datasets, respectively, in the FedSGD setting. Such gains in reconstructed image quality metrics are also maintained at higher batch sizes and in FedAvg settings. These results indicate that LoRA-based PEFT does not, by itself, prevent data leakage in FL, and carefully incorporated positional embeddings can help in exposing private information.

papers.title: The instanton sum in two-dimensional self-dual models
papers.summary: This paper considers the self-dual $CP^{N-1}$ model in two dimensions, which is defined by restricting the path integral of the ordinary two-dimensional $CP^{N-1}$ model to holomorphic configurations. We find that the instanton measure is one-loop exact and agrees with the one-loop instanton measure in the ordinary model. For the $N=2$ case, the instanton gas admits a description in terms of free massive Dirac fermions. Nevertheless, we find that the self-dual model is gapless. We also comment on the $θ$ dependence.

papers.title: Path-dependent triage: Early judgments lead conversational AI chatbots to miss mental-health emergencies
papers.summary: People increasingly bring mental-health concerns to consumer AI chatbots. In these conversations, clinically relevant information rarely arrives all at once. Instead, it unfolds over multiple turns, often in response to the questions the chatbot asks. Recognizing risk therefore depends on how a chatbot integrates newly disclosed information (inference) and on the questions it asks on each turn to elicit this information (context-seeking). Here we evaluated the conversational triage performance of 13 frontier AI chatbots tasked with engaging in 10-turn conversations with simulated users. Simulated users were grounded in one of 112 structured mental-health case files, each with an associated clinician-validated urgency level, from routine care to emergency. Chatbots failed to recognize one in five mental-health emergencies (20.3%), nearly four times the failure rate when all relevant clinical details were presented in a single message (5.6%). This gap was not explained by missing information: by the final turn, decisive facts had almost always been disclosed, and simply re-presenting those same facts as a single message reduced emergency under-triage to 12.1%. The problem lay instead in how the conversation unfolded, a phenomenon we refer to as path dependence. Early triage dispositions increasingly anchored later ones, such that emergencies missed early were rarely recovered as evidence accumulated. Context-seeking narrowed onto a small number of stereotyped questioning trajectories, with chatbots perseverating more than human clinicians given the same transcripts. Because the chatbot's running judgment shaped what it asked next, these two biases were plausibly coupled across turns. These dynamics are invisible to single-turn benchmarks but measurable in multi-turn evaluation, and point to concrete mitigations for safer conversational triage in consumer health AI.

papers.title: Slices for normal forms in quantum information and a Riccati-type equation
papers.summary: It is known that the normal space to an orbit of a compact group linear action meets each orbit. We show that this yields known normal forms for quantum states. We compute the gradient flow converging to the normal form and find it gives a Riccati type matrix-valued ODE.

papers.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

papers.title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
papers.summary: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types. Training reliable machine learning models for this task is difficult due to the variability and sparsity of whale calls in passive acoustic monitoring datasets. These difficulties are further amplified by time-varying noise that can mask whale calls and by site-specific ambient sound characteristics to which a trained model may not generalize. In this work, we present NAVE, a Conformer-based detector that improves whale-call detection via three components. First, its input representation combines per-bin complex mean subtraction, which suppresses constant site-specific ambient sound characteristics, with an additional per-channel energy normalization (PCEN) channel that adapts to temporal variations in the noise floor. Second, a frequency-dynamic stem processes these noise-aware representations with convolutions that adapt across the characteristic frequency bands of the target call types. Third, we use a Conformer backbone with a convolution kernel matched to the duration of the target calls that adds an inductive bias and improves temporal localization. We evaluate NAVE on BioDCASE 2026 Task 2 using leave-one-site-out cross-validation across the validation sites, which approximates deployment on unseen recording sites. A single NAVE model with a tuned per-class threshold exceeds the stronger WhaleVAD-BPN baseline, using no boundary-proposal network and no search over post-processing parameters. A controlled ablation study shows that the normalized front-end and a duration-matched convolutional kernel each contribute substantially to recovering the D downsweep, the hardest class for previous detectors, with the wide kernel giving the largest aggregate gain.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2026 Workshop. Code: https://github.com/TheFruitGuy/NAVE-SED
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 11th Workshop on Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE 2026), Boston, USA, pp. 1-5, 2026

papers.title: Efficient One-Shot Simulation of Network Instruments and Multi-party Purity Distillation
papers.summary: We undertake an information theoretic study of instrument compression problems (ICPs) in {multiple network} configurations, wherein the goal is to design and analyze protocols that simulate specific quantum classical (QC) correlation amidst distributed parties - some holding components of the quantum state and the rest holding classical registers - with minimum communication. We present a \textit{unified framework} of protocols based on likelihood instruments whose analysis yields new inner bounds in the one-shot and asymptotic regimes for the different network configurations we study. Our framework comprises of a common template for designing the instrument simulation protocol and analyzing its information theoretic performance. We also address a related problem of multi-party purity distillation wherein three distributed parties have to distil pure states efficiently via local operations and minimal communication. In regards to the tools, in addition to one-shot purity concentration protocol of \cite{202203arXiv_ChaPadSen} and one-shot quantum simultaneous decoder of Sen \cite{202102SAD_Sen}, we leverage Sen's fully smooth multi-partite covering \cite{202504arXiv_Sen} for all of our covering bounds.

papers.title: LACART: Lookahead-Augmented Collision Avoidance and Reference Tracking Strategies for Safety-Critical Robots
papers.summary: Autonomous racing provides a demanding testbed for collision avoidance under tight geometric and computational constraints. Building on a recent conference contribution and a master's dissertation, LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions (CBFs), a relaxed control Lyapunov function (CLF), and quadratic programming (QP) to modify nominal vehicle commands for obstacle avoidance and reference tracking. The method handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in a common optimisation layer. Comparative simulation results against Huang \emph{et al.} \cite{r9} show similar full-track paths and lower median computation times: 0.31 versus 0.33 ms per step and 0.023 versus 0.025 ms per QP solve. The dissertation further demonstrates a 1:43-scale vehicle with camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz control rate. We identify the conditions linking lookahead-point clearance to body clearance, illustrate hardware limitations, and propose a recorded demonstration of safety intervention and recovery. The contribution targets ground-robot collision avoidance and real-time safety monitoring.

papers.title: Are the tearing and the Weibel instabilities the same?
papers.summary: The tearing instability, which extracts free energy from a magnetic field gradient, and the Weibel instability, which draws free energy from temperature anisotropies, appear at first glance to be fundamentally distinct. However, the magnetic field gradient in the tearing instability requires a current, and the resulting plasma drift leads to an effective temperature anisotropy, so that the plasma is hotter along the direction of the current flow. This anisotropy can play an essential role in driving the instability. We demonstrate, using semi-implicit particle-in-cell simulations, a smooth transition between the tearing regime for thick current sheets, where the anisotropy has little influence, and a thin-current-sheet regime better described by Weibel physics. We find that for current sheet thicknesses less than the ion Larmor radius, where standard assumptions of the tearing instability break down, the growth rate of the mode commonly identified as the tearing instability agrees remarkably well with the growth rate predicted by ion-cyclotron theory, which is essentially the magnetized counterpart of the Weibel instability.

papers.title: Propagating the Hierarchical Equations of Motion using the Multi-Layer Multi-Configurational Time-Dependent Hartree method
papers.summary: The hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) are a powerful, numerically exact approach for simulating the time evolution of open quantum systems. Recently, several tensor-train- and tensor-network-based approaches have been suggested and realized to extend the range of applicability of the HEOM approach to larger and more realistic systems. In this paper, we build upon the existing twin-space formulation of the HEOM and present a novel approach to propagate the fermionic HEOM efficiently using the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree method (MCTDH). We benchmark the resulting HEOM+MCTDH method with electron transport calculations for a Holstein-type nanojunction model. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capabilities of the HEOM+MCTDH method by applying it to a more complex vibronic coupling nanojunction model with strong molecule-electrode coupling for which fully quantum simulations have not been feasible previously.

papers.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
papers.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.

papers.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
papers.summary: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model. One preference vector selects the adapter mixture that generates responses and weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. A single training run supports changing preferences at inference without further optimization. We experiment with four models on helpfulness and harmlessness and on solving math problems while following instructions. We also evaluate the two largest models on rewriting comments to preserve wording while reducing clues about personal attributes. On the first two tasks, LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy merging baselines across all four models. LambdaMix uses fewer training completions and stores fewer adapter parameters than a set of GRPO specialist policies. With architecture and initialization fixed, varying adapter mixtures and objective weights together gives wider score ranges and higher coverage than varying either alone.

papers.title: Turbulent wakes behind nine bluff-body shapes from direct numerical simulation and particle image velocimetry
papers.summary: We present a cross-validated dataset of turbulent wakes behind nine bluff bodies at Reynolds number Re = 10,000: a circular cylinder, a 2:1 elliptical cylinder at 0° and 90°, short and long isosceles triangles with the apex upstream or downstream, and a square cylinder at 0° and 45°. Each body was studied by wall-resolved direct numerical simulation (DNS) with a spectral-element solver and by time-resolved planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) in the MIT Intelligent Towing Tank. The DNS records contain time- and spanwise-averaged velocity, pressure and Reynolds stresses, 24-bin phase-averaged fields keyed to the lift signal, drag and lift histories, and one three-dimensional instantaneous snapshot per body; the PIV records contain the matching time-mean and phase-averaged fields in the same coordinate frame. The DNS set-up is verified against reference cylinder data at Re = 3900, and DNS and PIV at Re = 10,000 are compared field by field. The dataset supports the development and testing of data-driven turbulence closures, reduced-order models, and wake-stability analyses across geometries with distinct separation behavior.

papers.title: Dynamical gluon mass generation, the Schwinger mechanism, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and color confinement in the linear covariant gauges of QCD
papers.summary: We critically re-examine the Kugo-Ojima (KO) scenario for color confinement and identify several inconsistencies and a crucial error in its derivation. Within the KO framework, under customary assumptions, we show that the BRST quartet structure incorporates a unique mechanism for dynamical gluon mass generation -- namely, the Schwinger mechanism, in the formulation developed by Aguilar, Binosi, Ferreira, and Papavassiliou (ABFP). We show that the Schwinger mechanism is a Higgs mechanism, in that it occurs together with the spontaneous breaking of the global gauge charge, as it should. The ABFP bound state is the associated (unphysical) composite Goldstone boson. The zero-momentum value of the gluon propagator evaluated in the Pinch Technique--Background-Field Method (PT-BFM) naturally emerges in the derivation, setting a Renormalization-Group invariant scale for mass generation and suggesting a new nonperturbative interpretation of the PT-BFM. BRST symmetry takes over the role of the broken symmetry, while the color symmetry of the spectrum remains unbroken. We obtain a unique, well-defined, unbroken, BRST-exact asymptotic color charge operator that realizes the confinement of color in the sense of the absence of colored asymptotic states from the BRST cohomology. Still within the KO framework, we take the first fundamental step towards a proof of the nonperturbative unitarity of the linear covariant gauges of QCD, and we discuss the experimental evidence in favor of the Schwinger mechanism. We lay down the foundations for a unified theory of gauge-boson mass generation in the linear covariant gauges of Yang-Mills theories.

papers.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
papers.summary: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.

papers.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
papers.summary: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.
papers.comment: Submitted to Living Reviews in Relativity. 223 pages, 82 figures

papers.title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
papers.summary: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The algorithm is illustrated on the classical Hodgkin--Huxley neuron and on networks of up to 5000 neurons.

papers.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memory and planning. In this work, we address the problem of long-term memory in MBRL by moving beyond the commonly studied paradigm of architecture design. We introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), using gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of episode observations into world model parameters. This enables the agent to learn a distinct world model for each episode, improving memory capabilities compared to traditional approaches that solely rely on contextual memory. We first establish a proof of concept on a simplified two-dimensional variant of the Memory Maze environment, which we refer to as Memory Maze 2D, showing consistent improvements across different world model architectures. We then demonstrate the effectiveness of TT-MBRL in the 3D domain, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the Memory Maze benchmark. Finally, we show that TT-MBRL maintains strong performance on non-memory benchmarks such as DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.

papers.title: Entering a New Domain in the Era of Generative AI: An Autoethnography of Solo Game Development as a Bioinformatics Educator
papers.summary: The rapid improvement of generative AI (GenAI) not only increased the efficiency of practice but also empowered individuals with capabilities to explore new domains. However, identity formation in the wake of such empowerment remains understudied. We use an autoethnography to understand identity formation in the context of solo game development as a bioinformatics educator. With the goal of developing a create-your-own-adventure (CYOA) game, we collected data for 73 days through journal entries, interacting with communities of practices. The autoethnographer had continuously reassessed the situation, and closely interacted with communities of practice. Their prior knowledge was used to provide in-game context and to uniquely interpret game development processes. These findings suggest that the autoethnographer made efforts to belong to communities of practice and engaged extensively in sensemaking through the lens of a bioinformatics educator. Although GenAI puts power at hand, attaining a new identity took place at a human pace.

papers.title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
papers.summary: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
papers.comment: Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

papers.title: Quantum-walk measurements with sequential imaging of the same atomic sample
papers.summary: We demonstrate sequential single-atom-resolved imaging of the same ultracold atomic sample and apply this technique to quantum-walk measurements in an optical lattice. In quantum gas microscope experiments, fluorescence imaging provides microscopic information on atomic distributions but induces motional heating through photon scattering, making it difficult to reuse the same sample for subsequent quantum dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we apply Raman sideband cooling with parameters optimized for post-imaging cooling, enabling sequential single-atom-resolved measurements of the same sample. By optimizing the cooling parameters with machine learning, we achieve high fidelity over multiple imaging cycles. To demonstrate the capability of this technique, we measure one-dimensional quantum walks of single atoms in an optical lattice. By determining the initial atomic positions from fluorescence images, we extract quantum-walk transition probabilities without requiring deterministic preparation of the initial atomic positions. The observed dynamics agree with numerical simulations of quantum walks of single atoms. Our method provides a route toward reducing experimental overhead in quantum gas microscope studies requiring repeated acquisition of spatially resolved correlation data.

papers.title: CRTrack-Cap: A New Benchmark for Cross-View Dense Video Object Captioning
papers.summary: Dense video object captioning (DVOC) localizes, tracks, and describes object trajectories within a video. Existing methods process each camera view independently, producing separate camera-local tracklets and captions for the same person across cameras. These outputs lack a unified description and leave complementary appearance evidence across views unused. We therefore formulate cross-view DVOC (CVDVOC), which associates these tracklets into scene-level global trajectories and generates one caption for each trajectory from synchronized views. To support this task, we construct CRTrack-Cap from CRTrack by auditing text-identity links and converting usable referring expressions into canonical captions. It retains 425 global trajectories and 838 local tracklets across 13 scenes, with canonical captions for 335 identities. We adapt CHOTA to the cross-view setting as CV-CHOTA to jointly evaluate tracking and caption quality. Our reference framework combines View-Exclusive Cross-Camera Association (VECA) for grouping tracklets with Conflict-Evidence Gating (CEG) for integrating caption evidence using its reliability and disagreement across views. Against three single-view methods adapted with MvMHAT for cross-view association, our framework achieves CV-CHOTA scores of 83.43 and 33.48 on the scene-disjoint in-domain and cross-domain tests, respectively. Together, CRTrack-Cap and our framework provide a benchmark and a strong baseline for describing the same person consistently across camera views.

papers.title: SparseModesNet for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical system in heterogeneous porous media
papers.summary: Coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) models describe interactions among displacement, fluid pressure, and temperature in geothermal systems. Fine-mesh simulations over many time steps are costly, particularly with heterogeneous permeability and thermal conductivity or fracture networks that alter fluid and heat transport. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reduces the number of unknowns but can require many modes because its reconstruction is linear. We apply SparseModesNet to reconstruct coupled THM solutions using a small set of selected modes and a neural-network nonlinear decoder. Starting from a larger collection of candidate modes, SparseModesNet selects modes to reduce reconstruction error rather than simply retaining those with the highest energy. We compare SparseModesNet with POD on three problems: a two-dimensional heterogeneous medium, a two-dimensional connected fracture network, and a three-dimensional geometry based on Utah FORGE fractures. We evaluate reconstructed displacement, pressure, and temperature fields, as well as pressure- and temperature-based quantities of interest. We also test temporal interpolation by training on a subset of snapshots and reconstructing omitted snapshots within the same time interval. For the same reduced dimension, SparseModesNet achieves smaller reconstruction errors than POD and accurately recovers the solution fields and selected geothermal quantities of interest.

papers.title: ReplayAudit: Auditing Outsourced LLM Fine-Tuning via Sealed Records and Selective Replay
papers.summary: Auditing outsourced LLM fine-tuning requires checking an untrusted provider's training while controlling verification cost. Uniform sampling ignores training-time signals, while checking a suspicious record can require replaying several preceding steps. We present ReplayAudit, a telemetry-guided auditing system that seals training records before challenges and independently replays sampled intervals from sealed checkpoints. Loss changes and parameter-update norms guide stratified random sampling; replay determines whether the selected computation agrees with its records. We relate sampling probabilities to replay work and evaluate the system on real LoRA training. A 7B BF16 prototype rejects a false update-norm report during a random audit; targeted checks also reject false loss reports and skipped updates. We calibrate sampling budgets offline to at least a 90% probability of directly selecting an injected step. For two learning-rate deviation settings, executing these budgets on the same honest 1.5B trajectory reduces median complete-audit wall time by 49% and 67% relative to uniform sampling. When skipped updates evade the high-anomaly stratum, the corresponding audit instead costs 38% more. These results show how deviation capture and actual replay work jointly determine the cost of telemetry-guided auditing.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
papers.summary: We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $Λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.
papers.comment: 34 pages, 5 tables, 10 figures. SS, SG, AC, CS, and SMD contributed equally to this work and should be considered joint first authors

papers.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.summary: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Inspired by the model-based and environmental-wrench contributions to joint torques in floating-base dynamics, DKWBC uses inverse-dynamics feedforward and joint PD feedback to supply tracking torques, while a residual policy learns additional joint-torque corrections for balanced execution. By explicitly accounting for motion-dependent torque demands, this structure simplifies the policy's learning task.
