Experiments in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that a single learned balancing policy generalizes across motion datasets while maintaining accurate motion tracking and balance across ground support, attached payloads, and physical interaction. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DKWBC/.

papers.title: Quantum subsets discrimination and key sifting with success probability one
papers.summary: Non-distinguishability of non-orthogonal quantum states is the essential feature of quantum mechanics. In particular, one cannot deterministically orthogonalize the set of quantum states, while probabilistic orthogonalization is possible, including unambiguous state discrimination and discrimination between the subsets. Here, we propose a method for error-free subsets discrimination with significantly increased success probability, which may reach one even for non-orthogonal and linearly dependent input states. This method may be applied in quantum cryptography: An alternative basis reconciliation procedure is described, which may provide unit sifting probability even for a large number of bases and for non-orthogonal states within each basis.
papers.comment: 4 pages. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. A

papers.title: Dual-Region Slice Aggregation for CT-Based Renal Tumor Classification
papers.summary: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common kidney cancer in adults. We present a region-aware architecture for CT-based ccRCC classification. Tumor and 0--10 mm peritumoral context are pooled separately from shared frozen DINOv3 feature maps. A shared position-aware slice aggregator precedes fixed training-only principal component analysis (PCA). The resulting representations are fused with radiomics using two scalar feature gates. Evaluation on KiTS23 and 111 external cases yields internal test and external AUCs of 0.8078\pm0.0154 and 0.9094\pm0.0015. Compared with matched single-tumor readout, mean AUC increases by 1.50 and 2.34 percentage points, respectively. Early-PCA and reconstruction controls yield lower internal mean AUCs, while external AUC is similar for early and late PCA. These findings highlight the joint role of regional readout and slice aggregation in adapting frozen visual features to renal CT.

papers.title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
papers.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. Rubric as Teacher uses unreachable rubrics as privileged information for reward-gated on-policy self-distillation, and Rubric as Critic decomposes saturated rubrics into child rubrics that separate current responses while sharing the parent's weight. RuACT outperforms GRPO, rubric reweighting, and rubric-guided exploration on all four medical and scientific benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and achieves the best average with Qwen3-1.7B. On initially unreachable rubrics, unguided recovery rises from 35.02% to 42.86%, while child refinement improves reward-quality alignment on independent rollouts from 57.74% to 60.77%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/RuACT.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
papers.summary: Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $ρ$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log ρ$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.

papers.title: Magic Can Superactivate Quantum Capacity
papers.summary: Environmental magic can enable two channels with zero quantum capacity to transmit quantum information jointly. We establish this superactivation within a family of discrete quantum convolution channels with fixed Clifford interactions. For the couplings considered, stabilizer-mixture environments induce entanglement-breaking channels. We construct a mixed magic environment whose induced channel has positive private capacity and a Choi state with positive partial transpose, hence zero quantum capacity. A half-erasure auxiliary activates this channel through the Smith--Yard mechanism. Finite-block encoding and decoding over a self-complementary convolution auxiliary then realize a higher-dimensional erasure channel that still permits activation. We also bound the activated capacity by the modified relative entropy of magic of the main environment. Replacing either environment of the convolution pair by any stabilizer mixture makes the joint quantum capacity vanish, identifying environmental magic as a necessary resource on both sides for this realization.
papers.comment: 6 pages,1 figure, main results; detailed proofs and supplementary material to be added in a revised version

papers.title: Multi-Mode Pinching-Antenna-Based OFDM Systems: A Robust Design Perspective
papers.summary: A robust transmission framework is proposed for a multi-mode pinching-antenna (MPA)-based orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system under both channel state information (CSI) errors and PA positioning errors. A physical model is first developed based on the multi-mode coupled-mode equations (CMEs), which characterizes the frequency-dependent guided-mode propagation and the coupling among guided modes and PAs over the OFDM band. Based on this model, a worst-case sum-rate maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions under CSI and PA positioning errors, subject to user quality-of-service (QoS) and transmit-power constraints. To solve the resulting non convex problem, the worst-case CSI is exactly obtained for any given PA positions by solving trust-region subproblems, while the PA positioning errors are handled by grid-based and second-order approximation-based scenario constructions. Then, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed, where the baseband beamformer and the intended PA positions are updated via the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) method and successive convex approximation (SCA), respectively. Both subproblems are solved efficiently by exploiting the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) conditions. Numerical results show that the proposed robust design outperforms the non-robust and conventional robust benchmarks with the same multi-mode architecture in terms of both worst-case sum rate and QoS satisfaction. They also demonstrate that the proposed robust design satisfies the QoS requirements of all users more reliably than the baselines that consider either CSI errors or PA positioning errors.

papers.title: SQUALO II: Probing Accretion Through CO Molecular Outflows in Massive Star-forming Clumps
papers.summary: Molecular outflows probe protostellar accretion and mass transfer from clump scales to forming stars. We present an ALMA study of CO (J=2-1) outflows toward 13 massive clumps from the SQUALO sample, spanning a broad evolutionary range and exhibiting clump-scale infall. We identify 51 high-velocity CO lobes associated with 31 outflow systems and derive their physical and dynamical properties assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium. Outflow inferred accretion rates are typically 10^{-5}-10^{-3} Msun/yr, consistent with active massive star formation. The maximum outflow velocity shows little dependence on candidate driving-core mass, indicating that it is not a reliable tracer of protostellar mass in clustered environments. Outflow momentum flux correlates positively with clump surface density, whereas accretion rate shows a tentative, statistically nonsignificant decrease with increasing virial parameter. Total outflow inferred accretion rate shows a tentative positive relation with clump-scale infall rate but remains systematically lower, suggesting that the detected outflows represent only part of the large-scale mass flux. The clump L/M ratio moderately anticorrelates with projected outflow length, although projection, observational limitations, and the embedded source population prevent a unique evolutionary interpretation. Together with the continuum derived fragmentation properties, our results show that compact cores embedded within infalling clumps drive the outflows. The tentative relation between clump-scale infall and protostellar accretion suggests a possible connection across these scales, although our observations do not directly trace mass transfer from filaments to individual protostars.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables, Accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Extended Model-Based Learned Inertial Odometry
papers.summary: Inertial odometry is a compelling approach to state estimation for agile quadrotor flight due to its affordability, low weight, and robustness to perceptual degradation. However, relying only on integrated inertial measurements is impractical, as sensor errors and time-varying biases lead to significant pose drift. Although recent advances have enabled inertial odometry for drone racing, existing approaches show limited generalization to trajectories not seen during training. This work improves generalization by adopting a body-frame representation and incorporating body-frame torque dynamics into the learning pipeline. The learned model predicts short-horizon relative displacements, which are fused with IMU measurements in an Extended Kalman Filter. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the previous state-of-the-art learned inertial odometry approach for quadrotor pose estimation on unseen trajectories. An additional evaluation on four public quadrotor datasets, with whole trajectory shapes held out of training, confirms a lower velocity error on every held-out set and shows that the torque input is most informative when it is derived from the rotor signals. Code, data pipeline and trained models are publicly available.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
papers.summary: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory. The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.

papers.title: Scanning Probe Control, Quantum Dynamics, and Dispersive Readout of Suspended Carbon Nanotube Resonators
papers.summary: Suspended carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer promising opportunities for quantum nanomechanics owing to their small effective mass, strong electrostatic tunability, and mechanical nonlinearity. We develop a unified theoretical framework for coherent control and readout of a suspended CNT driven by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip and capacitively coupled to a Cooper-pair box (CPB). We first derive the linear and nonlinear Duffing response of the CNT and quantify the effects of AFM force gradients, tip-position fluctuations, and voltage noise on mechanical stability, dephasing, and heating. These results establish operating conditions for coherent actuation with limited backaction. We then quantize the Duffing oscillator, derive its Kerr anharmonicity, and identify the requirements for selective control of individual vibrational transitions. Estimates of thermal occupation and active cooling illustrate the constraints for CNT modes spanning frequencies from 54 MHz to 5.37 GHz. Finally, we derive the CNT--CPB interaction and its dispersive limit, showing how phonon number and parity can be mapped onto the CPB through Ramsey interferometry and detected using quantum-capacitance readout. The resulting framework identifies the conditions under which localized AFM actuation, nonlinear quantum dynamics, and superconducting state-resolved detection can operate within a single CNT device.

papers.title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
papers.summary: This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions. Therein, the non-conformity scores are normalized with an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on the log-transformed leave-one-out residuals of the base model. We show that the coverage guarantee of jackknife+ conformal prediction carries over to the adaptive intervals if the leave-one-out auxiliary models are trained on nested leave-one-out residuals. For fixed-basis polynomial chaos expansions fitted by ordinary least squares, all required quantities are derived in closed form and the guarantee-preserving adaptive intervals are obtained from a single model fit, without any model retraining. For sparse polynomial chaos expansions, where multiple model fits are necessary, we propose a heuristic simplification that limits the computational overhead of adaptivity at the cost of the formal coverage guarantee. Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset show that the suggested method attains the target coverage while providing intervals that adapt to local prediction uncertainty, therefore being considerably more statistically efficient. These advantages are particularly prominent in high-uncertainty regions of the input space, where the performance of non-adaptive methods degrades substantially.

papers.title: Quantum Interference Control of Coupled Atomic Spins
papers.summary: We propose a protocol for the non-resonant electric control of quantum states in atomic-scale spin systems using Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana (LZSM) interferometry. We focus on a Ti-Ti-Fe trimer on a thin MgO layer, a platform that has recently emerged as a promising candidate for qubit realization using electron spin resonance combined with scanning tunneling microscopy (ESR-STM). We first analyze a Ti dimer in the absence of the Fe atom and show, through a detailed spectroscopic study, that avoided level crossings can be engineered by combining the in-plane component of the external magnetic field, the tip magnetic field, and the applied bias voltage, which allows the system to be tuned electrically through these crossings. Based on this, we develop LZSM protocols for coherent state control in the dimer using non-resonant LZSM-STM. We then consider the full trimer, where the Fe atom generates a local magnetic field at the remote Ti atom, enabling non-local spin control. We show that this remote and non-resonant manipulation reduces unwanted effects associated with tunneling electrons and enables quantum operations on short timescales. Our results show that quantum interference can be used as a resource for electrically driven, non-resonant, and non-local spin control in atomic-scale systems. This approach enables fast quantum operations while mitigating decoherence, offering a promising route toward scalable atom-based qubit architectures.

papers.title: Expert Spindles in the Wild: Enriched Supervision for a Dense Detector
papers.summary: Sleep spindles are a hallmark of healthy NREM sleep whose frequency, amplitude, density, duration and topography vary with brain maturation, age and disease. Their manual annotation is impractical and variable between scorers, yet the public references used to train automatic detectors cover these characteristics only partially: stage N2 only, a single central derivation, or short pre-selected segments. Measuring duration and density requires dense detectors that learn event boundaries from annotated onsets and offsets, and therefore inherit the protocol under which those boundaries were scored. We introduce Expert Spindles in the Wild (ESW), a stage-agnostic expert spindle annotation set covering 19 complete MASS-SS2 recordings ($\approx$150 h of continuous EEG, 29,819 events). A sleep neurophysiologist annotated the recordings using the full EEG montage, blinded to sleep-stage labels and prior spindle annotations. On the 15 nights shared with historical scorers, ESW recovers 92.7% of E1 and 73.7% of E2 events, while recovering 81.6% of the MODA expert-consensus events on the common excerpts. Despite stage-blind annotation, 99.0% of ESW events occur in N2/N3. Used to train a fixed dense detector on a frozen SleepFM encoder, ESW reaches an event-level $F_1$ of 0.680 on 166 unseen MODA subjects, compared with 0.635 for E2 ($ΔF_1$ = +0.045, paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.024, 0.065]). ESW is thus useful supervision for cross-dataset detection, and closer annotation-level agreement with the MODA consensus did not translate into better transfer performance in this experiment. The annotations are released under the MASS data-use terms (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23894975).
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027 (under review)

papers.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
papers.summary: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. In a search for phonon-mediated superconductors, density-functional perturbation theory on 45 structurally novel designs gives isotropic Allen-Dynes critical temperatures above 10 K for 39; the highest is 24.0 K for ZrTiNb2CN3, and H4LiPd3 (23.2 K) lies on the static DFT hull. In searches for photovoltaic absorbers, SCAN calculations confirm ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull, and show that the systematic gap error of the training functional propagates into the designs unless the objective corrects for it. Quasiharmonic free energies from machine-learned potentials further show that finite-temperature competition with solid phases can reorder candidates relative to the static hull.

papers.title: Performance Bottlenecks in Computing ZK Proofs on a GPU
papers.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs allow one party to prove the correctness of a statement or execution of a computation while revealing no more than the statement of correctness itself. Recent use cases, such as AI datasets, suggest the need for faster proof generation over increasingly large constraint sets. This paper explores efforts in optimizing zero-knowledge proof generation, specifically PlonK, using GPUs, for applications that are not amenable to solution via incrementally verifiable computing (IVC). Our intention with this work is to improve ZK performance by introducing fundamental changes in the low-level architectural structure of proof generation. These changes affect performance curves for most current proof generation algorithms. In particular, this paper explores the trade-offs between increased parallelization on GPUs and the resultant memory management problems that occur due to this parallelization. We implement a parallelized PlonK in order to analyze these trade-offs and make arguments concerning the nature of data flows within the proving protocol. Our results lead us to consider multi-GPU environments to maximize performance for large circuit sizes. Such environments introduce issues of communication, efficient hardware management, data partition, and data transfers. This paper further discusses the use cases that motivate multi-GPU implementations, their cost models, and the use of remote direct memory access (RDMA) for data transfer among GPUs.

papers.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
papers.summary: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows. We introduce TurtLES, a 14 TB dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes in the shear-layer transition regime, computed via high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations. The dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with 3-11 million points per frame, spanning variations in geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack. Unlike existing datasets, TurtLES combines (i) physically realistic turbulence with an active energy cascade driven by vortex stretching, (ii) dense irregular meshes, and (iii) long-horizon temporal dynamics. We benchmark state-of-the-art neural operators on autoregressive rollouts and identify key failure modes, including temporal instability, loss of small-scale energy, and challenges in learning on large irregular domains. TurtLES provides a new benchmark for evaluating surrogate models on 3D turbulent wakes at industrially relevant mesh resolution.

papers.title: Circular interval-valued regression with application to wind direction: A cylindrical approach
papers.summary: Many real-world datasets are inherently interval-valued, yet standard statistical methods are typically designed for point observations. Furthermore, intervals that are circular in nature may naturally exist. In this paper, we introduce a cylindrical regression framework for interval-valued circular data, addressing the joint challenges of the periodical nature and measurement uncertainty within the observed circular intervals. The proposed model accommodates a circular interval-valued response variable and both circular and linear covariates using a centre-range approach. To estimate the model, a maximum likelihood approach is proposed. The performance of the proposed estimation procedure is demonstrated through a simulation study. Application to two real-world datasets from a wind farm in South Africa and a weather station in Brazil further substantiates the model's practical value.

papers.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
papers.summary: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.
papers.journal: A. Sharma, A. Suman, M. Anvari, M. Dev Shrimali, C. I. del Genio and S. Jalan, Eur. Phys. J. Spec. Top. 235, 7741 (2026)

papers.title: BQP-Complete Susceptibilities Observable at Ballistic Times in Local Quantum Dynamics
papers.summary: Local response measurements track how perturbations spread in quantum simulators and nonequilibrium many-body systems. Locality bounds constrain the propagation speed, but do not determine whether the response can distinguish computational outcomes at fixed measurement precision as the distance increases. Here we construct time-independent dynamics with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions in which a fixed single-site detector responds to a remote bond phase after a time proportional to their separation. The susceptibility has a positive lower bound independent of distance. With product-state preparations, estimating this susceptibility to constant additive accuracy is complete for bounded-error quantum polynomial time (BQP), with a decision gap independent of distance. Two source-phase settings give the susceptibility with a distance-independent shot count at fixed accuracy and confidence. Inverse-polynomially weak local couplings between the computational register and the chain carrying the excitation preserve the gap. The leading correction vanishes when exchanging the two internal states of the excitation reverses the interaction. Varying the source and observation time makes all bond phases locally identifiable near the zero-phase reference setting. We also prove a conditional quantum advantage for distribution-free response prediction.

papers.title: Lightweight Path-Aware Frontier Re-ranking for LiDAR-Based UAV Exploration
papers.summary: Autonomous 3D exploration with UAVs requires efficient target selection under limited flight time and onboard computation. In conventional Euclidean-distance-based frontier pipelines, geometric distance may poorly represent the actual collision-free travel cost in cluttered environments, leading to inefficient frontier choices. This paper presents a lightweight path-aware frontier re-ranking method for LiDAR-based UAV exploration. The method first retains a small top-N set of promising frontier candidates using a lightweight utility function and then applies time-bounded RRT* planning to estimate their feasible path costs for re-ranking. The path generated for the selected frontier is further reused for navigation to reduce redundant global planning. Experiments in three warehouse-like environments show that the proposed method consistently produces shorter exploration trajectories than conventional frontier baselines, with traveled-distance reductions of up to 14.1%, while reducing exploration time by up to 9.5% in two environments and remaining competitive in the third. The method maintains map detail comparable to the conventional OctoMap-based baseline, demonstrating an effective trade-off between exploration efficiency and mapping quality.
papers.comment: Accepted for presentation at RIVF 2026 (20th International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies)

papers.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
papers.summary: (Context) The X-ray spectra of magnetic cataclysmic variables (MCVs) with extreme magnetic fields, the polars, often exhibit a prominent soft X-ray excess attributed to buried shocks. (Aims) Using the first-ever high-state XMM-Newton observation of the highest field polar, AR UMa ($B\approx230$ MG), we established the source's accretion scenario and derived the energy budget at the magnetic extreme of MCVs. (Methods) Using X-ray, UV, and optical spectral and timing analysis, we disentangled the radiation components and located their origin in the binary. (Results) AR UMa showed one active ("southern") pole during our observation. The spectrum of the active pole was dominated by soft, blackbody-like emission with $kT_{\rm BB} \simeq 35$ eV and showed no evidence for an optically thin hard X-ray emission characteristic of a cooling post-shock accretion column. Instead, we find constant, faint, optically thin plasma emission with a temperature of $\approx 1$ keV at all orbital phases, which is uncorrelated with the soft X-ray emission, and we attribute this to shock-heated matter at the stagnation region. Pronounced absorption dips punctuate the phase of active X-ray emission and are associated with puffed-up material in the stagnation region. Using spectro-timing analysis of the absorption dips, the density profile and evolution of the clumpy flow were probed. We find evidence of a cyclotron harmonic from the southern pole (160 MG) near $\sim$2300 Angstrom in the UV spectrum. We report minute-long quasi-periodic oscillations in the optical, UV, and X-ray light curves. (Conclusion) AR UMa represents an extreme case of soft, blobby accretion, with an effectively infinite soft excess, extending the magnetic field range over which magnetic accretion can be studied by a factor of two. It is one of the rare systems in which X-ray emission from a stream-magnetosphere interaction is detected.

papers.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
papers.summary: Long-context language models often neglect information in the middle of the input, a phenomenon known as "lost-in-the-middle". Part of this gap may stem from the long-range decay of rotary position embedding (RoPE), which weakens the positional signal between distant tokens. Existing input compression deletes low-importance tokens, and attention reweighting acts only after RoPE has weakened this signal. RoPE-level methods modify positions directly but apply the same remapping to every query. To address these limitations, we propose QGPM (Query-Guided Positional Modulation), a training-free method that reshapes RoPE positions using query relevance from the model's own attention heads. QGPM builds a broad relevance map for lower layers and a sharp one for upper layers. Low-relevance tokens advance by less than one position on fast-rotating planes, pulling relevant evidence toward the query. Slow-rotating planes keep the original layout, with every token in place. Experiments on NoLiMa and RULER with multiple context lengths show that QGPM improves over base models and strong baselines, with the largest gains on retrieval tasks, and generalizes across multiple backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/iZHpy/QGPM.

papers.title: Risk-set reconstruction balance: zero-targeted diagnostics for artificial censoring in clone-censor-weight analyses
papers.summary: In clone-censor-weight (CCW) analyses, inverse probability of censoring weighting corrects selection from artificial censoring at protocol deviation. Balance diagnostics, such as the end-of-grace between-strategy standardised mean difference (SMD) and censoring balance, compare different populations, and their zero targets under a correct model are not formally stated. We show that, under positivity and a correct censoring model, the weighted retained individuals reconstruct the risk set before each censoring interval and the baseline population, and we propose risk-set reconstruction balance (RRB), which measures how far they depart from these two populations. Interval RRB has a zero target for every history function, including post-baseline covariates, for which between-strategy SMDs have none. Cumulative RRB keeps a zero target for baseline covariates after outcome events, whereas the end-of-grace SMD acquires a depletion term. In simulations, interval RRB responded to an omitted term's effect on censoring whether or not the term was prognostic. Under correct models, the exceedance rate of its studentised maximum over a null reference for chance imbalance was 3.5-6.0% (nominal 5%) when the censoring model pooled nine intervals and mostly 1.0-4.5% under censoring in a single interval. With many early events, cumulative RRB stayed near zero, whereas the end-of-grace SMD reached 0.40; under loss to follow-up that the weights ignored, cumulative RRB departed from zero and interval RRB stayed small. In a case study, interval RRB flagged a dispensing indicator outside the censoring model. Interval RRB checks the censoring model, and cumulative RRB the representation of the baseline population.
papers.comment: 18 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables; Supporting Information (16 pages) as ancillary file. R package and reproduction code: https://github.com/Nonokyu/ccwbalance (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24013295)

papers.title: A joint astrometric, eclipse timing and radial velocity orbit for the hierarchical triple V819 Herculis
papers.summary: We present a joint Bayesian orbital analysis of the hierarchical triple system V819 Herculis using ground-based astrometry, radial velocities (RV), and eclipse timing variations (ETV). By coupling these complementary data sets within a physically consistent Keplerian framework, we obtain a self-consistent three-dimensional solution for the outer orbit and the dynamical properties of the system. The outer orbit is found to have a period of $P_3 = 2016.97 \pm 0.27$ d and a high eccentricity of $e_3 = 0.6800 \pm 0.0016$, with the same orbital geometry simultaneously reproducing the sky-plane astrometry, the LiTE signal in the eclipse timings, and the tertiary radial velocities. The joint solution determines the component masses dynamically from these data alone, yielding $M_{12} = 2.721 \pm 0.055\,M_\odot$ for the inner binary and $M_3 = 1.954 \pm 0.070\,M_\odot$ for the tertiary, together with a LiTE amplitude of $A_\mathrm{LiTE} = 0.0104$ d and an RV semi-amplitude of $K_3 = 18.46$ km s$^{-1}$. The joint fit also yields an orbital parallax of $π_\mathrm{orb} = 14.08 \pm 0.13$ mas, consistent with Gaia DR3, Gaia DR2 and the HIPPARCOS New Reduction. The derived tertiary mass is higher than expected for a standard G8-type main-sequence star, suggesting that the tertiary component may be in an advanced evolutionary stage. The resulting outer orbit is well constrained, and the system is strongly hierarchical, with an outer period about 900 times the inner one. Finally, we provide predicted astrometric positions for the tertiary component for five years beyond 2026.5 to guide future high-precision observations.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 14 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables

papers.title: Relativistic analogue of the Kramers-Henneberger transformation and pair creation
papers.summary: In analogy to the Kramers-Henneberger transformation in non-relativistic quantum mechanics, we propose and investigate a spinor transformation for the Dirac equation which allows us to transform space-time dependent vector potentials $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}$_x away. In the mass-less case, we exactly arrive at the free Dirac equation, while for massive Dirac fields, the transformation results in a non-trivial mass matrix containing space-time dependent phases. Special emphasis is placed on the phenomenon of fermion pair creation in the external field $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}_x$ where the spinor transformation allows us to conceptually disentangle the different contributions to pair creation. It can also be used to reformulate the WKB approach and the Riccati equation (which can be advantageous in certain cases) and to obtain additional insight into the mechanism of dynamically assisted pair creation.

papers.title: Josephson current along the domain walls in Weyl fully compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl
papers.summary: We experimentally investigate Josephson current in planar Nb-Ti$_2$MnAl-Nb proximity devices, which are formed as junctions between superconducting niobium leads and single crystal flakes of the Weyl fully compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl. We demonstrate well developed Josephson effect for 2~$μ$m distance between the niobium contacts on the Ti$_2$MnAl surface. The measured critical current dependence on the magnetic field $I_c(B)$ shows strong anisotropy for two magnetic field orientations in respect to the Nb-Ti$_2$MnAl-Nb junction plane. For the parallel magnetic field, one can see standard Fraunhofer-like $I_c(B)$ suppression pattern. In contrast, $I_c(B)$ is qualitatively different in normal magnetic field, indicating non-trivial distribution of the Josephson current within the junction plane. From this anisotropy, long-range supercurrent and fast aperiodic fluctuations in $I_c(B)$ we conclude that Josephson current is transferred by the chiral surface states, which emerge along the domain walls in topological compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl. The conclusion on the domain walls is supported by magnetization data for small Ti$_2$MnAl flakes.

papers.title: Through Ups and Downs: the Transient Lensing Behaviour of SIDM halos undergoing Core Collapse
papers.summary: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes can become extremely dense following gravothermal core collapse, motivating their use as explanations for unusually concentrated gravitational lenses. Using an emulator calibrated on gravothermal fluid calculations, we investigate whether increasing central density necessarily strengthens lensing. We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $ρ\propto r^{-γ}$ with $γ\geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 11 figures. Submitted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
papers.summary: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.

papers.title: Sparse Array-Inspired Frame Structure Design for 5G NR ISAC
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. However, the extensive occupation of time-frequency resources for sensing limits the communication capacity. To address the resource conflict, this paper proposes a novel sparse sensing frame structure aligned with the 5G new radio (5G NR) resource grid at the slot and physical resource block (PRB) levels through a predefined sensing-pattern block. Specifically, inspired by the design of two-dimensional (2D) sparse antenna arrays, we map the sparse spatial geometries onto the time-frequency resource grid. By leveraging the hole-free property of the difference coarray, we eliminate the range-velocity ambiguity and cast the sensing signals into a reconstructed higher-order tensor representation. For efficient parameter estimation, we propose a novel binary-tree-based tensor train decomposition (BT-TTD) algorithm that extracts lower-dimensional tensor train cores (TT-cores) and executes a Vandermonde-prior-guided rectified alternating least squares (RecALS) algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme achieves competitive estimation accuracy with reduced complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the topological properties of various sparse patterns, revealing the inherent trade-off among sensing accuracy, resource occupancy, and computational complexity.

papers.title: Portable Glass-RPC Telescope for Muography and Future Applications at Laser Wake Field Accelerators
papers.summary: We report a 2025 beam test at ELBA, the multi-GeV laser wakefield accelerator at ELI Beamlines, using a Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) telescope with an active area of 16 * 16 cm2. The portable design sup- ports autonomous operation in challenging environments. Previous cosmic-ray measurements established its tracking capability for muography. During the campaign at ELBA, 30 f s long, 0.5 PW laser pulses in- teracted with a plasma target at a 0.2 Hz repetition rate, where a tungsten converter upstream of the beam dump enhanced muon production. This was the first deployment of an RPC telescope in a high-power laser environment. The detector remained operational in the presence of radiation and electromagnetic interference. Although parasitic running and limited statistics prevented definitive identification of beam- induced muons, the measurements offered insight into background activity and showed evidence of re- constructed tracks. They establish the feasibility of a dedicated campaign with controlled beam conditions and improved muon sensitivity. This contribution forms part of the International Muography Workshop 2026 proceedings.

papers.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
papers.summary: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can induce a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. Here, we answer this question systematically. We first construct an explicit model and prove that coupling to an environment can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system, even without such resource supply. We consider Lindblad master equations with (i) time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, (ii) time-translation covariance, and (iii) detailed balance---conditions that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. Our model satisfies these conditions, and the activation occurs in a stationary state of both the isolated and open systems. We give several implementations of this dynamics with a zero-temperature Gibbs environment, a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, and only short-range Hamiltonians, one of which exactly reproduces the time-crystalline periodicity. We then prove a no-go theorem: under (i)--(iii), activation can arise only from an environment-induced Hamiltonian term, not from dissipation. Our results show that time crystals can be activated in open systems without external resource supply and identify the physical requirements on the system and environment for this activation through our general no-go theorem.

papers.title: M-Estimation in Censored Regression Model under Endogeneity
papers.summary: This paper develops a general M-estimation framework for censored regression models under endogeneity. A two-stage estimation is proposed to address the issue of endogeneity in the first stage and the issue of censoring in linear regression models in the second stage. The issue of endogeneity is addressed via instrumental variables using the control function approach. The issue of censoring in linear regression models is addressed via M-estimation using a suitably defined class of loss functions yielding a class of estimators. Thus, the proposed general M-estimation framework nests several existing estimators as special cases for the respective loss functions. Moreover, this provides flexibility of accommodating a broad range of robust loss functions that have not previously been studied in the context of censored regression. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed class of estimators. An empirical study based on simulated datasets is conducted to illustrate general M-estimation for various choices of loss functions and to examine the finite-sample performance of various resulting estimators.

papers.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
papers.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $λ$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $λ\ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $λ\ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

papers.title: Graph representations of dislocation networks
papers.summary: The mechanical response of a crystal is governed by the evolving network of dislocations it contains, yet quantitatively linking the `state of that network' to its yield stress remains challenging. Here we represent the dislocation networks obtained from discrete dislocation dynamic simulation as graphs, using five distinct graph representations, characterize each network through a compact set of topological properties, and predict the yield stress from these graph properties and the applied strain rate using a standard random forest model evaluated with strain rate stratified cross-validation. The model predicts the yield stress with $R^2\approx0.86-0.90$ across all box sizes and $R^2\approx0.91-0.94$ for larger box sizes, and this accuracy is consistent across all five representations, indicating that the topology-stress relationship is a robust feature of the graph properties rather than an artefact of any single graph representation. We propose graph topology as a compact and robust route for connecting the microstructural state of a dislocation network to its mechanical response in addition to established variables.

papers.title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
papers.summary: One aspect of pangenome analysis that has received little attention is the recovery of the individual genomes that gave rise to a pangenome graph. While substantial effort has focused on constructing pangenomes from collections of genomes, the inverse problem remains largely unexplored: given a pangenome represented as a set of weighted adjacencies, can we reconstruct the constituent linear genomes that underlie it? Thus we introduce the pangenome peeling problem, which seeks to decompose a weighted adjacency graph into a collection of linear genomes whose combined adjacencies reproduce the observed edge weights. This problem is particularly relevant when considering ancestral pangenomes, where the graph structure may be known or inferred, but the underlying genomes are not. As a first step toward addressing this problem, we formally define pangenome peeling and derive a lower bound on the minimum number of genomes required to explain a given weighted adjacency graph. We then present two reconstruction methods: one based on the sequential addition of edges and a second based on extracting maximum-spanning-tree structures. Both methods produce genome collections that exactly explain the input adjacency data. To evaluate the recovered sets of genomes, we compare them to the set of input genomes using a maximum-weight matching framework based on the double-cut-and-join distance with indels. Here the maximum-spanning tree approach is superior, producing sets of constituent genomes close to the simulations while the sequential addition of edges approach yields constituent genomes increasingly divergent from the input as genomes sizes increase.
papers.comment: This is an extended version of the article of the same name submitted to the RECOMB 2027 conference

papers.title: Violent relaxation redux
papers.summary: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.

papers.title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
papers.summary: We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

papers.title: Secondary neutron beam production at Jefferson Lab
papers.summary: We investigate secondary neutron production by an 11 GeV electron beam in the Hall A beam dump at Jefferson Lab and their transport to a downstream experimental area. This secondary beam could operate opportunistically with the primary electron-scattering programme. The neutron energy spectrum extends from thermal energies to several GeVs, offering a distinctive opportunity for irradiation at energy grater than 1 GeV. We considered three configurations: the current setup, the planned BDX facility, and an optimized BDX layout with a dedicated neutron extraction pipe. We also studied how radiators made of different materials and placed upstream of the beam dump increase neutron production.

papers.title: The PICO-40L detector
papers.summary: The PICO collaboration has designed and constructed a novel bubble chamber to search for evidence of Weakly Interacting Massive Particles, a leading dark matter candidate. The PICO-40L detector is the successor to PICO-60, and uses a fully redesigned system for pressurization of the active volume after a bubble nucleation event. Pressure in PICO-40L is transferred to the target fluid through a set of two nested synthetic quartz vessels connected by bellows below the active volume. This is in contrast to the design of earlier detectors in which the pressure was transferred through a buffer fluid atop the target fluid, within a single synthetic quartz vessel connected to a bellows above the active volume. Removing the buffer fluid removes the potential for backgrounds arising from the interface between the two fluids, and moving the bellows below the target fluid suppresses potential backgrounds from particulates originating from the bellows. The newly designed detector concept of PICO-40L is referred to as the Right-Side-Up (RSU) design and requires a dedicated thermal system to keep the lower region of the detector cold while the upper region is stably superheated. The main goal of PICO-40L is to establish the performance characteristics of the RSU detector concept, which will inform the operating configuration of the final generation PICO dark matter detector, PICO-500, which is currently under construction at SNOLAB. This paper reviews the design, installation, and performance of the PICO-40L detector.

papers.title: Benchmarking Speaker Embedders in the Sub-Second Regime for Real-Time Voice AI Agents
papers.summary: Real-time Voice AI agents must separate the active user from intelligible background speech that survives conventional noise suppression. Background sources include television audio, family members, and colleagues. Production denoisers remove non-stationary environmental noise effectively. Background speech shares the spectral characteristics of the target and passes through, causing false acceptances in downstream speaker verification (SV) and automatic speech recognition (ASR). We benchmark open-source speaker embedders TitaNet-Large, TitaNet-Small, ECAPA-TDNN, CAM++, and SpeakerNet under a strict sub-second latency budget. Evaluation combines a controlled benchmark with a weighted human-annotated production set. Our controlled benchmark is built from real calls in which a second real speaker is injected into silence intervals at modulated amplitude. We report three findings. First, denoising before embedding is generally harmful and raises equal error rate (EER) across architectures. Second, truncating audio below the full voice-activity segment degrades every model. Third, roughly half of the TitaNet embedding is redundant for this task. Trailing dimensions encode population attributes such as language and gender. Such attributes carry little discriminative value in a demographically homogeneous user base. We distill these results into deployment guidance. Verification should run on raw audio with full voice-activity chunks. Thresholds should favor precision over F1. Truncated embeddings reduce the cost of similarity search.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at AIST 2026

papers.title: Moral Consumers and the Environment
papers.summary: We study the taxation of environmentally harmful goods when consumers have a Kantian desire to ``do the right thing''. A consumer evaluates her buying strategy, a rule that specifies whether to buy, by the material payoff she would obtain if others followed the same rule with a probability given by her degree of morality. Equilibrium exists and is unique in finite populations with heterogeneous morality. The optimal tax depends crucially on whether consumers are aware that tax revenue is returned to them. If they are, the Pigovian tax is optimal under homogeneous morality, whatever consumers know about environmental costs, and we give conditions under which it remains the unique optimum under heterogeneous morality. If they are not, the optimal tax is lower, and more so the more moral consumers are. Under a quota system such as the EU Emissions Trading System, any cap at least as stringent as the Pigovian quota admits an equilibrium in which morality has no effect on consumers who are aware of the system.

papers.title: Superconducting Fluctuation Driven Quantum Transport in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$ Thin Films
papers.summary: Superconducting fluctuations (SF), arising from Cooper-pair-driven interactions and electron-electron interactions within the transition regime, can dominate the magnetoconductance (MC) of superconducting thin films near their transition temperature. In some systems, this fluctuation-dominated regime is preceded by a narrow window in which quantum interference effects are manifested as weak antilocalization (WAL) or weak localization (WL). Here, we report magnetotransport measurements on thin films of the high-temperature superconductor Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$ (BSCCO) that establish SF as the dominant mechanism governing MC across the transition regime. In the narrow temperature window well above $T_c$ where SF does not exist, a cusp in MC can be attributed to WAL-like signature well described by the Hikami--Larkin--Nagaoka (HLN) framework. Closer to the transition ($T_{BKT}$), we observe signatures consistent with Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) correlations, underscoring that the dominant physics is set by collective, pairing-driven behavior rather than single-particle quantum interference. Measurements on non-superconducting control samples show no WAL-like features, indicating that the WAL over narrow temperature window, emerges only in conjunction with superconducting fluctuations. Hall measurements further reveal a concomitant sign reversal of the dominant carrier response, pointing to a substantial reorganization of transverse transport coincident with the onset of superconductivity. Together, these observations establish that magnetotransport in BSCCO thin film.
papers.comment: The Central Inferences and Figures of the paper have changed significantly compared to v1 of arXiv: 2511.00803

papers.title: Characterization of the Frequency-Current Curve of First-Order High-Pass Neurons
papers.summary: A spiking model, called the High-Pass (HP) model, has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable primitive. This model is composed of a static activation function, usually a sigmoid, in positive feedback with a high-pass filter. The HP model enters a tonic spiking regime whenever its input lies in the high-gain zone of the sigmoid, where the sigmoid's slope exceeds 1. In neuroscience, the frequency-current (FI) curve is the standard way of characterizing the tonic spiking regime of a neuron. So far, the FI curve of the HP model has been characterized analytically only for specific sigmoids, and has otherwise been computed through simulation. These simulations are computationally heavy, since simulating neurons requires solving a stiff system of differential equations. This paper bridges this gap by analytically characterizing the FI curve of the HP model with a first-order high-pass filter, for a broad class of sigmoid functions. The FI curve of the first-order HP model can be computed by solving two input-independent equations and evaluating two input-dependent integrals, with no need to simulate the model itself. A spiking primitive is said to be Type I (resp. Type II) if tonic spiking starts at a zero (resp. non-zero) frequency. This paper also shows that, for the HP model, the type depends solely on the local shape of the sigmoid at the outer edges of its high-gain zone. A sharp corner, where the derivative approaches a value strictly smaller than 1 from the outside, yields a Type I primitive. A locally twice differentiable corner, with a bounded second derivative and a derivative approaching 1 at the edge, yields a Type II primitive.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness and Limitations of Open-Weight LLMs for Low-Resource Offensive Language Detection in Danish
papers.summary: We study the effectiveness and robustness of open-weight large language models (LLMs) for Danish offensive language detection, an underexplored low-resource task. We evaluate four model families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen) across eleven prompting strategies spanning five design categories, cross-prompt generalization, Danish orthographic variation, and robustness under balanced and naturally imbalanced class distributions. We compare against three BERT-family baselines with distinct pre-training strategies, evaluated via both masked language model prompting and supervised fine-tuning. Even without task-specific fine-tuning, LLMs can surpass all three fine-tuned BERT baselines, and lightweight finetuning yields substantial further gains. No single model or prompt category dominates, underscoring that prompt design interacts with model pre-training in ways that cannot be predicted a priori. Semantically grounded prompts transfer more robustly, while format-constrained patterns consistently fail to generalize. ASCII transliteration of Danish-specific characters (æ, ø, å) generally degrades performance, indicating these characters encode meaningful signal. At the same time, the gap between a balanced test set (best F1 of 0.84) and the corpus's natural class skew (0.62 trained on skewed data, 0.70 trained on balanced data) -- relative drops of 26.2\% and 16.7\% -- shows that class imbalance remains a critical open challenge. Our code and configurations are available at https://github.com/PASHAADC/Danish-LLM-HateSpeech.
papers.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData 2026)

papers.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
papers.summary: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important for deploying evaluation metrics in real-world settings, where both input ambiguity and domain shifts are common. In this work, we propose an uncertainty-aware extension of the BEiTScore image captioning metric, producing conformally calibrated confidence intervals alongside alignment scores. Our approach models predictive distributions over human judgments, enabling both accurate scoring and principled uncertainty quantification in a single forward pass. We evaluate our BEiTScore++ metric across multiple benchmarks with human-annotated ratings, showing that it preserves the ranking correlation of BEiTScore, while producing intervals whose width tracks the prediction error more closely than Monte Carlo dropout on most benchmarks. The estimated uncertainty also grows under image degradation and on out-of-domain artwork images, making BEiTScore++ a practical tool for uncertainty-aware evaluation of image-caption alignment.
papers.journal: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026

papers.title: Selection versus residuals: deep-learning solvers for the Dubreil-Jacotin-Long equation and application to mode-2 internal solitary waves
papers.summary: Neural solvers offer structural flexibility for the Dubreil-Jacotin--Long (DJL) equation of internal solitary waves, which also admits the trivial state, oscillatory wavetrains and broadened near-solutions. A solver must select the physical wave before resolving it. Turkington's variational principle selects the wave through the nonlinearity of the available potential energy (APE). An exact virial partition shows that every localized wave carries more kinetic energy than APE, so a quadratic APE would favour a broadened field. The nonlinear APE enhancement, $1.27$--$2.06\times$ for the computed waves, reverses this ordering, although the preferred width remains weakly selected. From a shared KdV-derived start, a constrained Deep Ritz objective recovers the mode-1 wave, whereas strong- and weak-form residual objectives, which vanish at every exact solution and therefore do not favour the physical wave over other roots, lose the prescribed APE within one descent round. The recovered wave is under-resolved because its residual is dominated by high-wavenumber error that the energy barely penalizes, and a residual refinement at exact APE then meets every acceptance criterion. Structurally excluding mode 1 from the trial space, we compute mode-2 waves on four stratifications. A computed wave core qualitatively reproduces the two-lobe structure observed on the South China Sea shelf. In the deep basin, the selected core misses the residual criterion, and residual refinement widens it with little change in the energy objective. The two resolved linear estimates suggest weaker relative mode-1 radiation at larger ratios of wave half-width to resonant wavelength.

papers.title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection
papers.summary: Large language models enable fine-tuning-free spoken language understanding (SLU) through in-context learning, but direct query-based retrieval may select semantically similar yet intent irrelevant demonstrations. This paper presents Query-Adaptive Intent Detection via Prototype Extraction (APEX), a two-stage retrieval framework that first selects candidate intents using intent-level prototypes and then retrieves contextual exemplars within the selected intent space. Experiments on the SLURP dataset evaluate joint SLU performance using Exact Match Accuracy (EMA) under full-transcript and perplexity-stratified conditions, with additional retrieval analysis on ASR-generated transcripts. Compared with query-based retrieval, APEX improves EMA by 4.34 and 3.97 percentage points with Qwen3 4B and Gemma-3-4B, respectively, on full transcripts. Under high-perplexity inputs, APEX also yields EMA gains of 7.66 and 2.13 percentage points. Retrieval analysis further indicates that prototype-guided candidate selection achieves higher ground truth intent coverage across multiple input conditions.
papers.comment: Accepted for oral presentation at TAAI 2026. 6 pages

papers.title: CucumberVision at the Edge: Accuracy, Throughput, and Energy of RGB-D Cucumber Sizing on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 4
papers.summary: Non-contact fruit sizing from RGB-D imagery reaches sub-centimetre accuracy on workstation hardware, but in-field grading requires the same pipeline to run on a low-power single-board computer, and the cost of that transition is rarely reported. We deploy a curvature-aware cucumber length-measurement pipeline (YOLO26n detection, prompt-based segmentation and a medial arc spline estimator) on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and a Raspberry Pi 4, and characterize both against an RTX 3050 Ti workstation by replaying 50 identical greenhouse captures of 7 specimens, with specimen-level cluster-bootstrap statistics. Accuracy is preserved: mean absolute error (MAE) is 0.58 cm (95% CI 0.46-0.69) on both the workstation and the Jetson at matched precision, with a paired difference of zero. TensorRT FP16 compilation cuts Jetson detection latency 2.57x, giving two operating points on one board: 72 ms per fruit at 0.84 cm, or 2.74 s at 0.64 cm. Four ablations map the design space. For prompted segmentation backends, measurement accuracy is fixed by the backend and reproduces across platforms to within 0.01 cm, while its cost is fixed by the platform and varies 214x, so the two choices are separable. Whole-graph INT8 quantization of the NMS-free detection head fails structurally, returning no detections, because one output tensor carries both pixel coordinates and confidences; we show that no calibration strategy can avoid this. Excluding the head restores function at 1.37x. Energy per fruit is 42.2 J on the Jetson, and its 7 W mode consumes 73% more than its 15 W mode. The Raspberry Pi with MobileSAM costs 2.5x more per fruit than the Jetson with SAM despite drawing 47% less power, and it runs without thermal throttling under sustained load. The results define an accuracy-throughput-energy envelope with three non-dominated configurations and give rules for selecting among them.

papers.title: The ATAR, a dense and compact vertex detector for the PIONEER experiment
papers.summary: PIONEER is an approved experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland that aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons with an accuracy of 0.01%. This is an order of magnitude improvement in precision compared to its predecessors and approaches the accuracy of the standard model prediction. The key elements of PIONEER are a high resolution calorimeter built concentrically around the high granularity active target (ATAR). The ATAR is composed of a stack of 48 low gain avalanche strip detectors (LGADs) to stop the beam pions and provide detailed information of the event topology. This will include precise timing (in the order of 200ps), spatial information (to an accuracy of about 60 micro meter) and pulse height information with a high dynamic range to separate pion stops from muons and MIPs. To avoid affecting the energy measurement of the positrons, the readout electronics is placed outside the acceptance angle of the calorimeter. It is composed of a fast amplifier and a fast sampling chip digitizing the LGAD wave form for real time analysis. The paper describes the PIONEER-experiment with focus on the ATAR and its readout. The status of the development and activities in 2026 will be reported.
papers.comment: 34th International Workshop on Vertex Detectors, Jul 20-24, 2026 in Stoss, Switzerland

papers.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
papers.summary: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $γ$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $γ$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $γ$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2σ$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $γ$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

papers.title: Scalable Estimation and Inference for Varying Coefficient Expectile Regression with Streaming Data
papers.summary: Nonparametric expectile regression methods face new challenges from streaming data, where retaining the full dataset for batch processing becomes increasingly impractical. In this paper, we develop a scalable nonparametric expectile regression framework for varying coefficient models. We estimate the coefficient functions online via functional stochastic gradient descent with Polyak--Ruppert averaging in a product reproducing kernel Hilbert space, requiring only gradient information and one pass over the data. For this online estimator, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds, prove its optimal nonparametric convergence rate under the proposed step-size schemes, and derive its Berry--Esseen bound for pointwise asymptotic normality. To perform online inference for the varying coefficient expectile regression models, we propose a multiplier bootstrap procedure that perturbs the stochastic gradients with independent random weights and recursively constructs bootstrap trajectories. We establish the bootstrap consistency of the online inference procedure, yielding asymptotically valid pointwise confidence intervals. Simulation studies and a real data application confirm the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Thermal Field Theory for General Equilibrium Density Matrices
papers.summary: Thermal field theory (TFT) is the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. This (book) chapter provides a pedagogical introduction to (and a review of) TFT for general equilibrium density matrices, which allow arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. A general technique to compute ensemble averages is illustrated. Path-integral methods are developed to study the partition function and the thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all field theories of physical relevance.
papers.comment: Invited chapter of the Quantum Field Theory section of "Comprehensive Quantum Physics" (Elsevier); 28 pages

papers.title: A hair-thin implant opens the entire depth of the mouse brain to revisiting the same structures at subcellular resolution
papers.summary: Ultrathin multimode-fibre endoscopes provide minimally invasive access to subcellular structures throughout the depth of the mouse brain. Here we introduce a chronically implantable interface with a diameter of 144 μm, about the thickness of a human hair, that extends this capability to longitudinal imaging, enabling repeated access to the same fine structures over extended periods. The system supports weeks-long tracking of individual dendritic spines, allowing quantitative comparison of their dynamics and survival across dendritic compartments. We further demonstrate longitudinal intracellular calcium imaging during spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity in the same cells across days, as well as repeated measurements of blood flow in the same vessels across multiple brain regions. This chronic endomicroscopic platform provides stable, minimally invasive optical access for longitudinal subcellular-resolution imaging of brain structure, activity and blood flow across depth.
papers.comment: These authors contributed equally: Miroslav Stibůrek, Tomáš Pikálek, Petra Ondráčková Corresponding authors: Hana Uhlířová (huhlirova@isibrno.cz) and Tomáš Čižmár (cizmart@isibrno.cz)

papers.title: Resolving non-neutrality across scales in a hyperdiverse tropical forest
papers.summary: Different ecological processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Macroscopic regularities can therefore be captured by descriptions that ignore microscopic details, even when those details are mechanistically relevant to ecological processes. Here, we develop a framework inspired by statistical mechanics to track interspecific spatial correlations under spatial coarse-graining. To do so we combine random-matrix filtering with a spatially explicit neutral model. Applying this approach to eight censuses of the Barro Colorado Island tropical forest, we observe a continuous crossover from an interacting to an effectively neutral organization. Below a few tens of metres (20--35~m), the empirical correlation spectrum differs from neutral expectations, revealing scale-dependent species-specific structure. Part of this structure can be attributed to environmental heterogeneity. However, residual spatial associations provide candidate signatures of biotic interactions or other unmeasured ecological, non-neutral processes. With increasing spatial coarse-graining, empirical and neutral correlation spectra progressively converge, and above the crossover scale the neutral model provides an accurate description of the measured collective organization. Neutrality thus emerges as an effective description of the collective organization of the forest above a characteristic scale, without implying that species are equivalent at the individual level. Our framework provides an operational way to locate that scale.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 51 references and Supplemental Material
